title: The Tio brothers: language, looks and photographs
summary: Last questions about Louis and Lorenzo Tio: they spoke Spanish, English and French, and no photographs are known.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, before we stop, I don't want to keep you for another two or three minutes, but since there are none of the TOs left to speak for themselves and give us any of their history, if there's anything else you can think of, I don't like to keep harping on them, but I'd love one more in question. I'd love one more in final chance. Anything about, it was Louis Keough was your teacher. Don't worry about him. That's all, you won't make any. Can you remember, did he speak much English or did he speak much in Keough? Oh, yes, oh, yes, oh, yes, sure. Oh, yes, sure. Oh, yes, sure. Or was it Spanish if he came from Mexico?
They spoke Spanish, but they developed the English and French. Oh, yes, you'd never know. You'd never know that they weren't originally all these fellas.
Because I have heard sometimes people will imitate their talk a little bit, they'll use sort of the French accent.
Yeah, but they didn't even have the Spanish accent. They didn't even have that? No. But when you saw them, you know you were looking at a Mexican. They had, you know, they're a certain type.
I've never even seen a good picture of them. No? Lorenzo Jr., I've seen him. He had sort of long, black, wavy hair. Uh-huh. A real good-looking fellow. A great big fellow.
Oh, yeah, they both were. But how were they? And I can't, I don't know that I've ever seen a picture of the old man.
Were they fairly tall? Oh, I know. Somebody told me that Joe Oliver's the widow, Stella Oliver has one in New Orleans. I haven't had her. Is that so? So we'll get to see her, maybe she'll have one.
Are you on your way there from here?

I just came up from there. I'll be there, I'll only be here a week and I'll go back. I see. So I'll get to see her within a month or two now. And she had a picture of one of the Teos, either Louie or Lorenzo. You knew them both, I guess, then, fairly well, did you?
Oh, oh, yes, I should say, very well.
Your teacher was Louie. Yeah. Louie Teos. He's the one I think they usually call Papa Teos.
Yeah, that's right. That's right. Louie's the one we used to call Papa Teos. Yeah.

And the other was Lorenzo Sr., they call him now. And the Junior is the one that was with P. Rowland's band, went to New York, made Rutgers. Yeah. The others never made Rutgers. Well, unless there's something else you can think of about the Teos, I think we can-
